summary: The Positive Mass Theorem in general relativity
problem: As a cornerstone of mathematical general relativity, the Positive Mass Theorem asserts that for any complete, smooth, connected 3-dimensional
asymptotically flat Riemannian manifold with non-negative scalar curvature, the total gravitational (ADM) mass is non-negative, and vanishes if and only
if the manifold is isometric to flat Euclidean space \mathbb{R}^3. Landmark proofs of this theorem via minimal surfaces (by Schoen and Yau) and spinors (by
Witten) were central to the Fields Medals awarded to both Shing-Tung Yau (1982) and Edward Witten (1990). Using LEAP, we formalize this celebrated
theorem end-to-end by following the modern harmonic-function level-set approach of Bray, Kazaras, Khuri, and Stern (https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.06754).
title: Harmonic Functions and the Mass of 3-Dimensional Asymptotically Flat Riemannian Manifolds
